question: Netflix phone screen for a Software Engineer role. **Implement an in-memory cache with TTL (time-to-live) expiry.** Then **extend it to LRU eviction** when the cache is full, and finally **make it safe for concurrent use**. The reporter noted the concurrency part could be explained rather than coded. Variants of this question also ask you to write tests and to handle rolling (gradual) cache invalidation.
lookingFor: Clarifying requirements first: API (get/put/delete), capacity, TTL per key or global, time source.
Choosing the right data structures so get and put stay O(1).
Correct expiry semantics, including lazy versus active cleanup.
Awareness of concurrency hazards and a sensible locking strategy.
Testability, for example an injectable clock instead of real sleeps.
followUps: How would you avoid a cache stampede when a hot key expires?
What are the trade-offs of a global lock versus lock striping?
How would you test the expiry logic without sleeping?
How would you extend this to a distributed cache?
